topic.name: EGFR-mutant lung cancer: resistance to osimertinib
topic.question: New evidence on how EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer becomes resistant to osimertinib, how often each mechanism occurs, and what works after resistance.
topic.primary_query: (EGFR[tiab] OR "ErbB Receptors"[mh]) AND (osimertinib[tiab] OR AZD9291[tiab] OR Tagrisso[tiab]) AND resistan*[tiab]
topic.secondary_query: ("Drug Resistance, Neoplasm"[mh] OR "acquired resistance"[tiab] OR "disease progression"[tiab] OR progressed[tiab]) AND ("third-generation"[tiab] OR "third generation"[tiab] OR T790M[tiab] OR C797S[tiab] OR "EGFR-TKI"[tiab] OR "EGFR TKI"[tiab]) AND (NSCLC[tiab] OR "lung cancer"[tiab] OR "lung adenocarcinoma"[tiab])

criteria.text: Concerns EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer: patients, tumour samples, cell lines or animal models.
Involves osimertinib (also called AZD9291 or Tagrisso), alone or in combination.
Reports on resistance to osimertinib: a mechanism, how often a mechanism occurs, or treatment after resistance.
Reports original data (trial, cohort, case report, laboratory study) rather than being only a review, editorial or guideline.

fields.text: The resistance mechanism the paper describes, genetic or not, in the paper's words, e.g. MET amplification, ERK/GATAD2A/SAA1 axis, histological transformation.
Specific genetic alteration(s) reported, as written in the paper, e.g. EGFR C797S, MET amplification. Null if the mechanism is not a genetic alteration.
Context of the alteration, e.g. in cis or in trans with T790M, co-occurring alterations.
Treatment line or setting, e.g. first-line osimertinib, after progression.
Study design, e.g. retrospective cohort, phase 2 trial, case report, cell-line study.
Number of patients, if stated. Digits only.
What kind of finding the paper reports. Exactly one of the allowed values.
The main result in one sentence, staying as close to the paper's wording as possible.

high_impact.why: A result on what to give after resistance can change treatment, so a person always reads it. Mechanism papers are checked like any other and reach a person when a check fails.

paper.title: ENPP1 inhibits the cGAS-STING pathway to mediate immune evasion in EGFR-TKI-resistant non-small cell lung cancer.
paper.abstract: Third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), such as osimertinib, have demonstrated promising clinical efficacy in the treatment of EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Despite substantial progress with EGFR-TKIs, the development of acquired resistance remains a major clinical challenge. Notably, the addition of immune checkpoint blockade after TKI resistance has not resulted in significant survival benefits compared to chemotherapy. In this study, we performed a comprehensive transcriptomic analysis of established osimertinib-resistant tumor models and found that the expression of the ectonucleotide phosphodiesterase ENPP1, a key regulator of extracellular cGAMP signaling, was significantly upregulated in resistant tumors compared to the parental TKI-sensitive NSCLC tumors. Mechanistically, upregulated ENPP1 in resistant cells promoted the hydrolysis of extracellular cGAMP, suppressing the cGAS-STING pathway in immune cells and subsequently impairing immune cell activation and function, thereby promoting immune suppression and tumor progression. Genetic depletion or pharmacological inhibition of ENPP1 enhanced immune cell-mediated cytotoxicity against TKI-resistant tumor cells. Furthermore, the use of ENPP1 inhibitors both in vitro and in vivo enhanced immune cell activity and antitumor efficacy in TKI-resistant lung cancers with high ENPP1 expression. Importantly, these observations were further validated by paired clinical tumor samples, which demonstrated increased ENPP1 expression following the development of acquired EGFR-TKI resistance. Collectively, our study highlights a critical role for ENPP1 in mediating immune evasion through suppression of the cGAMP-STING pathway in the tumor immune microenvironment, supporting ENPP1 as a promising therapeutic target to enhance immunotherapy efficacy in EGFR-TKI-resistant NSCLC.

paper.title: Epigenetic Silencing of ZNF471 Contributes to Osimertinib Resistance in Lung Adenocarcinoma: β-Hydroxybutyrate Associates with ZNF471 Re-Expression and Reduced Resistance-Associated Phenotypes.
paper.abstract: Background: Acquired resistance limits the benefit of osimertinib in epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), and epigenetic silencing may contribute to this process. This study aimed to determine whether promoter hypermethylation-associated silencing of zinc finger protein 471 (ZNF471) contributes to resistance and whether β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) can restore ZNF471 expression. Methods: ZNF471 expression and promoter methylation were analyzed in public datasets, clinical samples, and osimertinib-sensitive and resistant cell lines. Functional assays and signaling analyses were performed in vitro, and BHB treatment and ZNF471 overexpression were evaluated in xenografts. Results: ZNF471 was downregulated and hypermethylated in LUAD, and low expression was associated with advanced stage and poor survival. ZNF471 restoration reduced the osimertinib half-maximal inhibitory concentration, inhibited migration, invasion, and tumorsphere formation, and was associated with suppression of PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling, whereas ZNF471 knockdown had the opposite effect. BHB increased ZNF471 expression, reduced methylation-specific PCR signals, and synergized with osimertinib in resistant cells in vitro. In xenografts, BHB treatment and ZNF471 overexpression each inhibited tumor growth. Conclusions: ZNF471 is an epigenetically silenced modulator of osimertinib sensitivity in LUAD. BHB may enhance osimertinib response by reactivating ZNF471. ZNF471 is an epigenetically silenced modulator of osimertinib sensitivity in LUAD. BHB may enhance osimertinib response by reactivating ZNF471. Taken together, these findings suggest that BHB is associated with ZNF471 re-expression and reduced osimertinib resistance-associated phenotypes in LUAD cells, although whether ZNF471 is required for this effect remains to be determined.

paper.title: Transformation to Small-Cell Lung Carcinoma and Then to Sarcomatoid Carcinoma in an EGFR-Mutant Lung Adenocarcinoma Patient During Systemic Therapy: A Case Report.
paper.abstract: This case exemplifies stepwise histological transformations of an initially EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma driven by tumor lineage plasticity under therapeutic pressure. Initial resistance to osimertinib manifested as transformation to combined small-cell lung carcinoma, associated with concurrent TP53/RB1 co-inactivation and the acquisition of an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) C797S mutation. Subsequent progression after chemotherapy featured a rare sarcomatoid transformation, with the tumor retaining the original EGFR Exon 19 deletion, supporting clonal evolution. This phenotypic shift, indicative of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), may have been associated with PTEN loss and potential activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. The serial emergence of neuroendocrine and sarcomatoid phenotypes underscores the critical need for rebiopsy to guide therapy and highlights the profound adaptability of EGFR-mutant tumors, which remain a major therapeutic challenge.

paper.title: Pharmacological targeting of ANO1/TMEM16A in cancer: from channel inhibition to protein downregulation.
paper.abstract: Anoctamin 1 (ANO1/TMEM16A) is a calcium-activated chloride channel increasingly recognized as a compelling pharmacological target in oncology. Beyond its role in chloride flux, ANO1 has also been proposed to exert signaling-associated or scaffold-like functions in selected malignancies, including head and neck, breast, and lung cancers. Although pharmacological studies have progressed from broad inhibitors to selective probes and natural products, a critical need has emerged for a rigorous standard to evaluate these agents. A central challenge is distinguishing acute conductance blockade from protein-level downregulation, as these mechanisms may produce distinct biological outcomes. Channel inhibition suppresses ion flux while potentially leaving ANO1-associated protein complexes intact, whereas protein reduction may affect both conductance-dependent and signaling-associated functions; however, the extent to which these functions are mechanistically independent remains incompletely established. Consequently, regulation of ANO1 stability is emerging as a promising therapeutic strategy in tumors with high ANO1 expression and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) activation. However, in clinically relevant EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer models, the role of ANO1 should be interpreted cautiously. Current evidence supports ANO1 as a context-dependent preclinical vulnerability rather than an established mechanism for overcoming osimertinib resistance. To address methodological inconsistencies in the field, this review summarizes ANO1 cancer pharmacology and proposes a conservative operational evidence framework. By establishing strict validation criteria, we classify ANO1 modulators into functional inhibitors, dual modulators, protein-level downregulators, and protein-stability modulators while defining evidence requirements for bona fide targeted degrader designation.

paper.title: FLAURA2 - a step forward in first-line treatment of advanced EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer.
paper.abstract: Background: Activating mutations in epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) represent one of the most important therapeutically targetable alterations in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Osimertinib has become a first-line standard of care due to its efficacy, favorable safety profile, and activity in the central nervous system. Nevertheless, most patients eventually experience disease progression during treatment, and searching for strategies that further prolong disease control and delay the emergence of resistance remains an important clinical need. The FLAURA2 study evaluated the combination of osimertinib with platinum-based chemotherapy and pemetrexed in previously untreated patients with locally advanced or metastatic EGFR-mutated non-squamous NSCLC. Compared with osimertinib monotherapy, combination treatment demonstrated a significant prolongation of progression-free survival, and in the final analysis, also a statistically significant improvement in overall survival, with a median of 47.5 months vs. 37.6 months (HR for death 0.77; 95% CI 0.61-0.96; P = 0.02). Aim: The aim of this review article is to summarize the FLAURA2 study and its main clinically relevant results in patients with advanced EGFR-mutated NSCLC treated in the first-line setting. The text describes the study design, characteristics of the study population, and treatment arms, focusing on the efficacy outcomes of osimertinib combined with platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy compared with osimertinib monotherapy, particularly in terms of progression--free survival, overall survival, and intracranial efficacy. The review also includes a summary of the safety profile of the combination treatment and the main conclusions of the published analyses of the study.

paper.title: Epigenetic regulation of cancer stem cell plasticity and relapse competence in EGFR-mutant lung cancer.
paper.abstract: Cancer stem cell (CSC) plasticity is increasingly linked to therapy resistance, yet CSC identity is still often inferred from persistence, stemness markers, or short-term regenerative assays. EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer is a useful setting in which to examine this problem because residual states can be sampled before stable resistance is established. Here, we focus on how chromatin remodeling, DNA methylation, histone regulation, RNA epigenetics, adaptive signaling, metabolism, and the immune microenvironment influence stem-like behavior during EGFR-targeted therapy. We assess the literature using four evidence levels: state association, functional enrichment, post-treatment durability, and lineage-resolved acquisition of durable CSC function. The available data strongly support epigenetic regulation of therapy-persistent and resistant states, and several models show functional overlap with CSC-associated phenotypes. What remains largely missing is direct evidence that a prospectively identified persister lineage later acquires serially propagating CSC function. Minimal residual disease may therefore represent a period in which relapse-competent states are present but not yet irreversibly established.

paper.title: Reversal of acquired osimertinib resistance by YAP inhibition in lung cancer is associated with lipid metabolic reprogramming.
paper.abstract: Osimertinib (Osi), as the third-generation epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI), has demonstrated remarkable efficacy in the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, recent studies have found that its acquired resistance severely limits its therapeutic effect. This study shows that YAP activation is associated with lipid metabolic reprogramming in Osi-acquired resistance, providing new insights into overcoming this clinical challenge. In H1975/OR cells, YAP phosphorylation was decreased and nuclear translocation was increased, indicating YAP activation. Inhibition or knockdown of YAP significantly re-stored Osi sensitivity. YAP upregulated the expression of sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1 (SREBP1), fatty acid synthase (FASN), and stearoyl-CoA desaturase (SCD1), and promoted the synthesis of triglycerides, cholesterol, and phospholipids. Lipidomics revealed that YAP inhibition reduced multiple phospholipids. Furthermore, inhibition of YAP downregulated the anti-apoptotic protein B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL2) and enhanced Osi-induced apoptosis. This study firstly links YAP activation to lipid metabolic reprogramming and reveals its crucial role in Osi-acquired resistance. These findings not only deepen the understanding of the EGFR-TKI resistance mechanism but also provide a new therapeutic strategy for clinically overcoming Osi-acquired resistance. Targeting the phospholipid synthesis pathway mediated by YAP may effectively reverse the acquired resistance of NSCLC to Osi.

paper.title: Overcoming EGFR Resistance by Monovalent and Bident Inhibitors Targeting Cys775.
paper.abstract: Covalent targeting of EGFR cysteine 797 by osimertinib is one of the most successful breakthroughs in targeted therapy, fundamentally transforming the treatment landscape for non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients. However, resistance driven by the mutation of C797 remains a major clinical challenge. Developing novel covalent strategies beyond C797 targeting presents a compelling opportunity for next-generation EGFR inhibitors. We first demonstrated that cysteine 775, located deep within the ATP-binding pocket, is accessible by a rationally designed covalent molecule ZNL-3, which as the first-in-class covalent cysteine 775 inhibitor exhibited strong efficacy in osimertinib-resistant mouse models. To further enhance resilience to resistance-causing mutations, we developed a dual-warhead, bident compound YNW-1 which covalently targets both cysteines 775 and 797 simultaneously. YNW-1 is the first intramolecular lock to exhibit balanced reactive efficiency on both cysteines, rendering single-site mutations ineffective at conferring resistance. This study establishes the therapeutic potential of an EGFR covalent inhibitor through unprecedented targeting of cysteine 775. It also provides the first evidence that dual-cysteine engagement offers superior efficacy to conventional covalent inhibitors by delaying the emergence of resistance. Further optimization for clinical translation is currently ongoing in our laboratory.
